thesis: Black Stone Minerals, L.P. (NYSE: BSM) is a publicly traded Delaware limited partnership that owns oil and natural gas **mineral and royalty interests** across 41 U.S. states, plus smaller **non-operated working interests**. **[Fact]** The partnership receives revenue when third-party operators produce hydrocarbons from its acreage; it does not operate wells. **[Fact]** As of February 20, 2026, **212,333,793** common units and **14,711,219** Series B cumulative convertible preferred units were outstanding (`10-K_20260224_rpt20251231_acc0001621434_26_000018.htm`). **[Fact]** FY2025 total revenue was **$469.9 million**; net income was **$299.9 million** (**$1.28** per common unit basic); cash distributions to common unitholders were **$285.7 million** (**~$1.35** per unit on a weighted-average basis). **[Fact]** The asset base spans **20.3 million** net mineral and royalty acres (**2.6 million** developed, **17.7 million** undeveloped) and **527,366** net working-interest acres as of December 31, 2025 (`same 10-K`, Acreage tables).
why_market_wrong: Yield-focused investors may treat BSM as a simple commodity distribution bond and underweight the **17.7 million net undeveloped mineral acres** that require no capital from the partnership when third parties drill. **[Inference]** K-1 partnership tax reporting and a large unit count (~212 million) can exclude the name from dividend screens despite a **~9.7%** trailing distribution yield at **~$13.88** per unit. **[Inference]** FY2025 revenue rose **8.4%** year over year even as oil volumes fell **9.6%**, because natural gas realizations improved and lease bonus income rose **71%**; the market may anchor on peak 2023 distributions (**~$1.90**/unit) rather than the gas-weighted mix today. **[Inference]** Horizon Kinetics held **~151,238** units (~**$2.3 million** 13F value) as of Q1 2026 per the royalty screen; that is **context only**, not an approved third-party IRR input.
